**To Whom It May Concern,**  

I’ve collaborated closely with Xander de Vries 87 over the past two years at Lumina Labs, a small-scale startup focused on industrial automation. As a peer, I’ve observed his day-to-day contributions to data-driven decision-making and his role in shaping our predictive maintenance models.  

Xander’s strength lies in his ability to distill complex system behaviors into actionable features. Last quarter, he led the design of a feature engineering pipeline for sensor data, which reduced false positive rates in our anomaly detection models by 12% without requiring additional hardware. His approach balances statistical rigor with pragmatic implementation, ensuring models align with operational constraints. He also mentors junior engineers, often leading brainstorming sessions to refine feature selection criteria.  

One standout example came during a project to optimize energy consumption in manufacturing lines. Xander spent three weeks collaborating with engineers to identify latent patterns in vibration data. By incorporating time-series features that captured subtle degradation trends, he improved our predictive accuracy by 18%, enabling proactive maintenance and saving an estimated $25k in downtime. His work ethic is equally notable—he consistently prioritizes cross-functional collaboration, ensuring data science outcomes directly inform business strategy.  

In summary, Xander is a reliable, analytical collaborator whose technical depth and communication skills make him an asset to any team. His ability to translate statistical insights into operational value is rare in practice.  

Sincerely,  
[Your Name]  
Co-founder, Lumina Labs
